evidence.quote:
Patterns of expressed genes in the peripheral blood mononuclear cells of persons who were
receiving RTS,S/AS01 or RTS,S/AS02 malaria vaccine and were undergoing experimental challenge with mosquito-
borne falciparum malaria were examined to identify markers associated with protection.

At 5 days after challenge, differential expression
of genes associated with programmed cell death distinguished between subjects protected and not protected from
malaria blood-stage infection.

The RTS,S is a subunit recombinant vaccine expressed
in yeast that represents the central repeat and C-ter-
minal portion of the Plasmodium falciparum circum-
sporozoite protein (CSP) covalently linked with the S
antigen of hepatitis B virus [1].

Gene chip–based
prediction strategies have received approval from the US Food
and Drug Administration as prognostic tools for breast cancer
[17–22].

RMA is a method of normal-
ization of microarray data that leverages gene expression as-
sessments made on Affymetrix gene chips.

P p .05
Real-time polymerase chain reaction.

To conﬁrm obser-
vations from the gene chip data, TaqMan Gene Expression
Assays (Applied Biosystems) were used to detect genes in the
immunoproteosome pathway (PSME2, PSMB9, PSMB6, and
PSMA4) in 3 randomly chosen samples from protected and
nonprotected persons, at 2 weeks after the third vaccination.

GSEA and conﬁrmation by reverse-transcriptase polymerase
chain reaction.

Cutaneous delayed-type
hypersensitivity (DTH) in a multi-formulation comparator trial of the
anti-falciparum malaria vaccine candidate RTS,S in rhesus macaques.
